Task: Improve the understandability of the test `MullerSolverTest.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/local_workplace/commons-math/commons-math-legacy/src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math4/legacy/analysis/solvers/MullerSolverTest.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

Now I'll write the improved test. The main understandability problem is the repeated 4-line boilerplate (mutable `min/max/expected/result/tolerance` locals + a duplicated tolerance formula) appearing 8 times. I'll extract a single, well-named helper that captures the "solve on an interval and assert the root" intent.Compiles cleanly (`COMPILE_OK`). I refactored the eight repeated `min/max/expected/result/tolerance` blocks into a single well-named `assertRootFound` helper, named the `100` literal `MAX_EVAL`, and added intent-revealing comments — all while preserving the exact solver calls, arguments, and expected outcomes.
